2. This appeal, under Section 23 of Railway Claims Tribunal Act, 1987, has been filed against the judgment dated 15/3/2019 passed by the Railway Claims Tribunal, Bhopal Bench, District Bhopal in Case No.OA/IIu/BPL/2013/525 whereby the interest on the award amount has not been paid.

entities.text: Railway Claims Tribunal, Bhopal Bench, District Bhopal
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 3. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that interest was required to be paid but learned tribunal failed to order in this regard, therefore, appeal may be allowed and necessary order with regard to the interest may be passed.

She has placed reliance in the case of Union of India vs. Rina Devi ; AIR 2018 SC 2362, it is held in para 8(iv) which reads as under :
"(iv) Award of interest :- The Act is silent about the interest.

entities.text: Union of India vs. Rina Devi ; AIR 2018 SC 2362
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In Thazhathe Purayil Sarabi versus Union of India, this Court held that the CPC could be invoked and interest awarded at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of application till the date of award and 9% p.a. interest from the date of award till the date of payment.

entities.text: Thazhathe Purayil Sarabi versus Union of India
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In Mohamadi versus Union of India interest at the rate of 9% was awarded without any difference between the date of application and date of award or for subsequent award."

sentences.text: Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent drawing attention of this Court towards para 7 of the order dated 21/2/2024 passed by a co-ordinate Bench of this Court in M.A.No.1932/2022 (Bharat Gond & Anr. vs. Union of India) submits that provision of payment of interest is discretionary and is not and cannot be bound by rules.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Relevant para is extracted as under :
"7.
(vi)- As a general rule the rate of interest would be the simple rate of interest being granted by nationalized banks on fixed deposits for one year at relevant point of time.

(vii)-Above principles are applicable to compensation awarded under both Motor Vehicles Act & Railway Claims Tribunal Act."
4.
Heard rival contentions of learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
5. It is not in dispute that Railways Act, 1989 no provision has been made regarding payment of interest while awarding compensation.

6. Hon'ble the Apex Court in the case of Union of India (Supra) para 8(iv) has observed that in such situation CPC could be invoked and interest be awarded at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of application till the date of award and 9% p.a. interest from the date of award till the date of payment.
7.
In the judgement relied upon by learned counsel for the respondent some principles have been summarized in para 7 regarding discretion of the tribunal in regarding interest.

8. It is not in dispute that payment of interest is discretionary but looking to the beneficial legislation, regarding payment of compensation to the victims of the accident, in considered opinion of this Court, interest must be given as per judgement in Union of India (Supra).
